c.tagline: Moravia's baroque secret, crowned by Europe's tallest Holy Trinity Column.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis lack a uniform color and can overcharge tourists in the center; using the Bolt app or calling a reputable dispatch company is safer and cheaper.

emergency.note: 112 works for all emergencies; 158 reaches the police directly and 155 reaches ambulance services.

hood_desc: The city's grand main square, dominated by the UNESCO-listed Holy Trinity Column and the Olomouc Astronomical Clock with its distinctive communist-era mosaic. Baroque facades, the town hall tower, and fountains surround the pedestrianized plaza. It's the natural starting point for any visit.

A second historic square just steps from the upper one, centered on the ornate Caesar Fountain and the Church of the Holy Trinity. By night it turns into the city's main nightlife strip, with pubs and wine bars spilling onto the cobblestones. It stays lively year-round thanks to the large student population.

A modern residential and commercial district anchored by the Šantovka shopping and entertainment complex. It's popular for its riverside park, cinema, and everyday shopping away from the tourist crowds. Good transit links make it an easy, if less atmospheric, place to stay.

A quiet, workaday neighborhood near the main train station, with modest housing and local eateries. It sees few tourists but offers a real slice of Olomouc daily life and easy access to arriving trains. Rents and lodging tend to be cheaper here than in the center.

A leafy, riverside residential pocket bordering the Bezruč Gardens, a favorite park for locals to jog and picnic along the Morava River. It's a peaceful base a short walk from the historic core, with tree-lined streets and few crowds.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 4:30am-11:30pm, with a reduced night bus network
transit.pay: Contactless bank-card tap-in/tap-out or the Olomouc city transport app; paper tickets from machines at major stops
transit.note: Trams are the backbone of the network and connect the train station to the historic center in about 10 minutes

train: Olomouc hlavní nádraží is a major rail junction with frequent EC/IC trains to Prague (~2h15), Ostrava, and onward to Vienna or Warsaw
bus: RegioJet and FlixBus coaches link Olomouc to Prague, Brno, and Ostrava

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory; state the total you want to pay aloud rather than leaving cash on the table.

food.name: Olomoucke tvaruzky
food.desc: The pungent ripened cow-milk cheese made only near Olomouc, served in rings with raw onion, paprika and vinegar as a beer snack.

places.name: Svatovaclavsky pivovar
places.note: The city brewery restaurant serves a proper tvaruzky board alongside its own unfiltered lagers.

places.name: Hanacka hospoda
places.note: Regional Hana cooking on the lower square, with tvaruzky in several traditional preparations.

places.name: Olomouc Trznice market
places.note: Buy them fresh from Lostice producers at the covered market, cheaper than any restaurant.

food.name: Smazene tvaruzky
food.desc: Tvaruzky breaded and deep-fried until molten, cut through with tartar sauce and boiled potatoes; the most approachable way to meet the cheese.

places.name: Restaurace Moritz
places.note: Popular local brewpub with its own beer and a reliable fried-cheese plate; usually needs booking.

places.name: Svatovaclavsky pivovar
places.note: Large brewery hall pouring house lager and wheat beer, a natural match for fried tvaruzky.

places.name: Restaurace Drapal
places.note: Old-school pub famous for tank Pilsner Urquell and unfussy Czech classics since the First Republic.

food.name: Svickova na smetane
food.desc: Beef sirloin under a silky root-vegetable cream sauce with bread dumplings, cranberries and a spoon of whipped cream; the Czech Sunday dish.

places.name: Hanacka hospoda
places.note: Home-style version in a regional tavern on the lower square, generous with dumplings.

places.name: Restaurace Drapal
places.note: Traditional pub kitchen doing the classic without modern reinvention, at fair prices.

places.name: Vila Primavesi
places.note: Refined take served in a restored Art Nouveau villa with a garden terrace.

food.name: Gulas s knedlikem
food.desc: Thick beef goulash darkened with paprika and onion, ladled over bread dumplings and topped with raw onion rings; pub food at its most Czech.

places.name: Svatovaclavsky pivovar
places.note: Brewery goulash cooked with the house dark lager, served in a big vaulted hall.

places.name: Restaurace Moritz
places.note: Long-standing student and local favourite, with its own beers brewed on site.

places.name: Restaurace Drapal
places.note: Unpretentious tank-beer pub where the goulash is the standard order with a pilsner.

food.name: Vepro knedlo zelo
food.desc: Roast pork with bread dumplings and braised cabbage, the Hana region's staple plate, usually finished with caraway and a slick of roasting juices.

places.name: Hanacka hospoda
places.note: Built around Hana regional cooking, so this is the house speciality rather than a menu filler.

places.name: Svatovaclavsky pivovar
places.note: Large portions and house beer, popular with families and easy to walk to from the astronomical clock.

places.name: Restaurace Drapal
places.note: The everyday pub version locals actually eat, with both red and white cabbage.

food.name: Hanacke kolace
food.desc: Flat Moravian pastries from the Hana plain, topped with quark, poppy seed and plum jam and scattered with crumble.

places.name: Olomouc Trznice market
places.note: Bakery stalls sell them by the piece in the morning, still warm.

places.name: Kavarna Konvikt
places.note: Cafe in the baroque Konvikt art centre, good for pastries with coffee between galleries.

places.name: Cafe 87
places.note: Well-loved city cafe known for its cakes and chocolate pie, an easy sweet stop.

food.name: Olomouc craft lager
food.desc: Unfiltered lagers and dark beers brewed inside the old town, poured fresh from tanks a few metres from where they were made.

places.name: Svatovaclavsky pivovar
places.note: Brewpub with copper kettles in the room and a tasting flight of its own light, dark and wheat beers.

places.name: Restaurace Moritz
places.note: The other in-town brewery, with a garden and consistently well-kept beer.

places.name: Restaurace Drapal
places.note: Not a brewery but famous locally for tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell poured the traditional way.

food.name: Slivovice
food.desc: Moravian plum brandy, distilled across the surrounding countryside and drunk neat and room-temperature as a shot before or after a meal.

places.name: Hanacka hospoda
places.note: Regional tavern that stocks small-batch Moravian distillates alongside the food.

places.name: Restaurace Drapal
places.note: Classic pub setting for a shot with a beer chaser, the way locals order it.

places.name: Olomouc Trznice market
places.note: Stalls and nearby shops sell bottles from small regional distilleries to take home.

landmarks: Holy Trinity Column
A 35-meter baroque plague column so lavish it earned UNESCO status, crowding Upper Square with gilded saints and its own chapel.
Town Hall and Astronomical Clock
Olomouc's Gothic-Renaissance town hall bears a rare socialist-realist astronomical clock whose mosaic proletarians parade at noon.
St. Wenceslas Cathedral
A soaring neo-Gothic cathedral whose 100-meter southern spire is Moravia's tallest, built where young King Wenceslas III was murdered in 1306.
The Baroque Fountains of Olomouc
Seven monumental fountains starring Caesar, Hercules and Arion turn the old town's squares into an open-air sculpture gallery.
Archdiocesan Museum and Přemyslid Palace
Romanesque palace windows and a dazzling collection of ecclesiastical treasures, including a gold-encrusted carriage, beside the cathedral on Wenceslas Hill.
Dolní náměstí (Lower Square)
The quieter twin of Upper Square charms with the Marian plague column, two baroque fountains and pastel burgher houses.
Church of St. Moritz
A fortress-like Gothic church whose tower climb rewards with the best old-town panorama, and whose Engler organ is among Europe's mightiest.
Svatý Kopeček (Holy Hill) Basilica
A grand pilgrimage basilica gazes over the city from a wooded hill, paired with Olomouc's popular hillside zoo nearby.
Bezruč Gardens and City Walls
Parkland winds beneath the surviving medieval and baroque fortifications along the Mlýnský stream, prettiest in spring bloom.
Villa Primavesi
An Art Nouveau gem built for the banking family who patronized Klimt and Hoffmann, showcasing Viennese Secession elegance in Moravia.

train.note: Olomouc sits on the main Prague-Ostrava corridor, which is one of the busiest international rail routes in central Europe - EuroCity and Railjet services to Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Warsaw all pass through. Prague takes about 2h15 with ČD, RegioJet and Leo Express all competing. The station is east of the centre, linked by tram. Book ahead for the cheaper fares.

bus.note: Coaches use the terminal beside the main railway station. RegioJet and FlixBus run to Prague, Brno, Ostrava and onward into Poland and Austria; the train is generally faster on the Prague corridor. Carry your passport or EU ID card.

ferry.note: Czechia is landlocked and the Morava river at Olomouc is not navigable, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Kroměříž
half.blurb: A UNESCO-listed archbishop's chateau with Baroque gardens is about forty-five minutes from Olomouc.

half.name: Bouzov Castle
half.blurb: A neo-Gothic castle used in Czech fairy-tale films stands roughly forty minutes northwest of Olomouc.

half.name: Šternberk
half.blurb: A hilltop castle overlooks this small river town about thirty minutes north of Olomouc.

half.name: Litovel
half.blurb: A canal-laced small town nicknamed the "Haná Venice" sits roughly twenty-five minutes from Olomouc.
